analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING: 1) Thoughts from the Floor, 2) 2027 Global FX Outlook, 3) Equities Update and 4) Week Ahead Previews 16 Nov 2026
key_insights: GS rates desks say the market now prices a full Fed hiking cycle again, with peak terminal rate around 4.75% by next fall. About 1.5 hikes were added after the CPI report, and the market is reluctant to take any back on softer PPI components.

Short Macro Trading (Bingham) says 2027 pricing has shifted from an even spread through Q3 to a front-loaded path of hikes in Q1. He sees the front-loading as more likely than not to continue given no near-term progress on inflation and a pivot by the Trump administration away from escalation into November.

Bingham sees near-term policy risks skewed to the upside into the Dec SEP, with a presumptive increase in the 2027 dot from 4.125. He sees little reason to fade the knee-jerk retracement, but says terminal rate pricing is precarious and will react sharply to any wobble in AI sentiment. His preferred expression is receiving structures such as SFR H7H8.

USD Rates Vol (Korapaty) says another strong core CPI print would have added hike pricing regardless of Waller's comments. He does not expect a 50bp hike in December because there will not be enough data or FOMC votes, but data and Fedspeak have laid groundwork for hikes at consecutive meetings rather than quarterly.

Korapaty's base case is two additional hikes and then a pause, which reverses the 75bp of cuts from last year. This assumes core inflation gradually moves toward target over the next year. He puts the end of the current adjustment at 4.25-4.5% and neutral at 3.75-4%, where he thinks policy already is.

US Swaps Desk (Xholi) reads the market's refusal to take back hikes on softer PPI as positioning. Many investors chased the rally on AI capex slowdown fears and are now cutting those positions. He thinks a December hike is done, does not expect 50bp (only 27 is priced), sees terminal pricing above where the Committee ends up, and calls U7 a buy.

The Thoughts from the Floor key questions cover Fed pricing and terminal rate after CPI, the baseline for US data-centre gigawatt production in 2026-28 and how much is at risk after the mid-term political shift, whether the recent US inflation trajectory is broad enough to challenge GS's benign inflation outlook, and whether investors remain in the Brazil trade.

GS FX Strategy expects the Dollar to give way to a softer path over 2027 as its recent supports (stubborn inflation, resilience to higher energy prices, AI investment expectations) turn from a boost to a drag. Near term it expects mixed performance with some further Dollar strength, particularly against DM currencies.

GS forecasts EUR/USD at 1.08 in 3 months on near-term Euro pressure, then 1.15 by end-2027 on more resilient growth, fading headwinds and synchronized policy. It forecasts EURGBP at 0.86 in 12 months on easing European sovereign credit stress, and GBPUSD at 1.34 over the same horizon on energy relief and AI capex deceleration.

GS expects JPY to appreciate in 2027 as deep undervaluation erodes, with room for sharper gains if AI-related risks materialize. Its economists see three more 25bp BoJ hikes to 2% by June 2027 against around 1.75% priced, and forecast USDJPY at 158, 155 and 150 in 3, 6 and 12 months.

In Asia FX, GS sees USDCNY moving toward 6.30 by end-2027 and expects KRW, TWD and MYR to outperform. It expects the CBC to tolerate more TWD appreciation, SGD and THB to moderately underperform other low yielders, and IDR to underperform further with the MSCI decision pending. It maintains long MYRTHB and long INRIDR recommendations.

US Equity Derivative Sales (Coppersmith) says equities can grind higher after the positioning reset but recommends being more selective. It would use weakness in parts of AI to add rather than chase rallies, expects rotation beyond infrastructure into next year, and says AI spending growth is peaking with financing getting more expensive, so it would stay disciplined on hedges.

GS PB data show Tech was the most net-sold sector globally again last week, and the US Info Tech long/short ratio fell to its lowest in the dataset going back to 2016. CTA positioning in NDX is near max short, so GS says it would not take much to squeeze higher.

GIR expects new data centre capacity coming online in 2028 to be roughly in line with 2027 even in a bearish scenario, because so much construction is underway. The question is how much growth slows, not whether the buildout stops.

Week ahead US data and events: Retail Sales Tuesday (GS +0.3%, consensus +0.2%, last +0.8%), FOMC Minutes Wednesday, UoM inflation expectations Friday (GS 3.3%, consensus 3.4%, last 3.4%). Fed Chair Warsh speaks Monday and a heavy Fedspeak schedule runs through Friday.
GS expects Nvidia to deliver solid 3Q results on Tuesday with 4Q guidance above the Street on better-than-expected margins. Its 3Q and 4Q EPS estimates are both 6% above the Street.

Week ahead international: Eurozone CPI Wednesday in line with consensus (core 2.5% y/y, headline 4.0% y/y), UK CPI Wednesday with GS above consensus (core 2.90% vs 2.8%, headline 3.73% vs 3.6%), Japan October core CPI Friday, NBH on hold at 5.50% Tuesday and SARB on hold at 7.25% Thursday.
Trump, Xi and Putin are scheduled to meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen on Thursday.

tension_points.bull_case: Rates desks see a full hiking cycle to around 4.75% as justified by strong core CPI and hawkish Fedspeak. Bingham sees front-loading of 2027 hikes continuing and favors receiving structures only on AI-driven wobbles.
tension_points.bear_case: Xholi thinks the terminal rate is priced above where the Committee ends up and reflects positioning. Korapaty puts the end of the current adjustment at 4.25-4.5% and neutral at 3.75-4%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A wobble in AI sentiment, which Bingham says terminal pricing will react to violently, or a softer inflation trajectory.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is washed out. Tech is the most net-sold sector, the US Info Tech long/short ratio is at its lowest since 2016 and CTAs are near max short in NDX, so a squeeze higher needs little.
tension_points.bear_case: AI spending growth is peaking and financing is getting more expensive, so GS would stay disciplined on hedges and expects rotation beyond infrastructure.
